introduction-why-one-cluster-is-not-enou.core: Organisations run many clusters for blast-radius isolation, regional latency and data residency, scale limits (nodes, etcd size, API load), environment separation, compliance boundaries and upgrade safety. Multi-cluster brings challenges: consistent configuration, cross-cluster service discovery and traffic, identity and fleet lifecycle.

first_principles.problem: A single giant cluster's control-plane issue or bad upgrade takes down every team and region.
truths: One cluster is one failure domain.

analogy.title: Branch offices instead of one giant headquarters
analogy.story: A fire or strike at one doesn't stop the whole company.
analogy.breaks: Branches can run independently; multi-cluster apps still need cross-cluster coordination.

example.title: Cluster topology
flow: GitOps syncs all from one repo

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Failures and upgrades contained per cluster.

check.q: Name two reasons to run multiple Kubernetes clusters.
check.a: Blast-radius isolation and regional latency/data residency (also scale limits, environment separation, safer upgrades).

federation-the-meta-cluster-concept.core: Federation treats many clusters as one logical target: a control layer distributes resources with placement and overrides (e.g. KubeFed historically, now Karmada, Open Cluster Management, Fleet), and some tools provide cross-cluster scheduling and failover. Full federation adds complexity; many teams prefer GitOps fan-out plus multi-cluster service discovery.

first_principles.problem: Deploying the same app to 20 clusters with slight per-region differences is repetitive and error-prone.
truths: Most config is shared, some differs.
A meta-control-plane is another thing to run.
derivation: Or use **GitOps ApplicationSets** for simpler fan-out.

analogy.title: Head office issuing one policy to all branches with local addenda
analogy.story: The core rules are shared; each branch adds its local details.
analogy.breaks: Head offices don't fail over branches automatically; some federation tools can reschedule workloads across clusters.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: One Deployment, replicas split across two clusters.

check.q: What three concepts do federation systems generally use?
check.a: Resource templates, placement policies and per-cluster overrides.

gitops-architectures-hub-and-spoke-vs-in.core: GitOps keeps desired state in Git and agents reconcile clusters to it. Hub-and-spoke runs one central Argo CD managing many clusters (single pane of glass, but a central dependency with broad credentials). Independent (pull) runs an agent in each cluster (Flux or Argo CD per cluster), which is more resilient and secure but harder to view centrally.

first_principles.problem: A central Argo CD outage blocks deployments to all 40 clusters.
truths: Central components are dependencies and targets.
Pull-based agents need only outbound access.
derivation: **Independent**: agent per cluster, pull from Git.

analogy.title: One air traffic control tower for all airports versus a tower at each
analogy.story: Central is simpler to oversee; local towers keep working if the centre fails.
analogy.breaks: Towers communicate by radio; GitOps agents only need Git and their own cluster.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: Every prod cluster gets its regional overlay.

points: Git is the source of truth.

check.q: What's the main risk of hub-and-spoke GitOps?
check.a: The central controller is a single dependency and holds credentials to every cluster.

service-mesh-federation-connecting-servi.core: Multi-cluster meshes (Istio multi-primary or primary-remote, Linkerd multicluster, Cilium Cluster Mesh) connect services across clusters with shared trust (common root CA for mTLS), cross-cluster service discovery and locality-aware load balancing with failover. Kubernetes' Multi-Cluster Services API (ServiceExport/ServiceImport) standardises discovery.

first_principles.problem: Services in the EU cluster can't call the US cluster's payment service securely or fail over to it.
truths: Identity must be shared to trust across clusters.
Locality reduces latency; failover adds resilience.

analogy.title: Allied embassies with mutual ID recognition
analogy.story: Diplomats from one embassy are trusted at another and can be redirected if one closes.
analogy.breaks: Embassies negotiate trust politically; meshes need careful certificate management.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: EU callers use EU payments, fail over to US when unhealthy.

code.text:
trafficPolicy:
  loadBalancer:
    localityLbSetting:
      enabled: true
      failover: [{from: eu-west-1, to: us-east-1}]
  outlierDetection: {consecutive5xxErrors: 5, interval: 10s, baseEjectionTime: 30s}

check.q: What's required for mTLS to work across clusters in a mesh?
check.a: A shared root of trust (common root CA) so workload certificates are mutually trusted.

cluster-api-and-fleet-provisioning.core: Cluster API manages Kubernetes clusters declaratively from a management cluster: Cluster, MachineDeployment and control-plane objects with infrastructure providers (AWS, Azure, vSphere, bare metal) create, upgrade and scale clusters the same way Deployments manage Pods. ClusterClass templates standardise fleets.

first_principles.problem: Creating and upgrading 50 clusters with scripts and console clicks produces snowflakes.
truths: Clusters can be declared as objects.
derivation: **Upgrade** by changing versions; CAPI rolls machines.

analogy.title: A factory that builds identical franchise kitchens on order
analogy.story: You submit a spec; the factory builds and maintains each kitchen.
analogy.breaks: Factories ship once; CAPI keeps reconciling clusters after creation.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: A full cluster from a manifest; upgrades are a version bump.

code.text:
clusterctl init --infrastructure aws
clusterctl generate cluster prod-eu --kubernetes-version v1.31.2 \
  --control-plane-machine-count 3 --worker-machine-count 6 > prod-eu.yaml
kubectl apply -f prod-eu.yaml

check.q: What does Cluster API's management cluster do?
check.a: Runs controllers that create, scale and upgrade workload clusters from declarative objects.
